mean: without a moment's thought, answering on the spot
lit: not borrowing (needing) any thinking or searching

use.how: Adverbial before a verb of answering, saying or writing: 他不假思索地回答。 Can praise quick fluency or hint at rashness, depending on context.

near.diff: 毫不犹豫 is acting without hesitation, from resolve; 不假思索 is responding without stopping to think at all.
脱口而出 is words slipping out, often ones you regret; 不假思索 is the speed of the reply, not the slip.

cue: The teacher asks a hard question and one student fires back the answer instantly, without pausing to think. How did she answer?

ctx.s: 老师一提问，她就{不假思索}地说出了答案。
ctx.en: As soon as the teacher asked, she gave the answer without a moment's thought.

ctx.s: 问他最喜欢哪座城市，他{不假思索}地说：“当然是成都！”
ctx.en: Asked which city he likes best, he answered on the spot: "Chengdu, of course!"

ctx.s: 这些字他练了上千遍，现在能{不假思索}地写出来。
ctx.en: He has practised these characters a thousand times; now he can write them without thinking.

ctx.s: 面试官问你为什么想来，你最好别{不假思索}地随口回答。
ctx.en: When the interviewer asks why you want to join, better not to answer offhand without thinking.

ctx.s: 借钱这么大的事，你应该好好想想，怎么能{不假思索}就答应了？
ctx.en: Lending money is a big deal; you should have thought it over. How could you agree without a moment's thought?

ctx.s: 记者话音刚落，部长便{不假思索}地给出了明确答复。
ctx.en: The reporter had barely finished when the minister gave a clear reply on the spot.

bad.s: 这个问题太难了，我{不假思索}了很久。
bad.en: (meant: I thought about it for a long time)
bad.why: It means answering with no thought at all, so it cannot describe long thinking.

bad.s: 我昨天{不假思索}他的生日，真不好意思。
bad.en: (meant: I forgot about his birthday)
bad.why: It is not 'forget' and takes no object; it describes how quickly someone answers or acts.

use.how: Describes a person's manner toward someone, often someone more powerful: 他的态度不卑不亢。 Also adverbial: 不卑不亢地回答。

near.diff: 落落大方 is natural, unselfconscious ease in company; 不卑不亢 is keeping one's dignity before power or pressure.

cue: Facing the company's powerful chairman, a young engineer neither flatters him nor talks down, but calmly states her view. How was her manner?

ctx.s: 他见了老板也{不卑不亢}，大家都很佩服他。
ctx.en: Even in front of the boss he is neither servile nor arrogant, and everyone admires him.

ctx.s: 面对客户的刁难，她{不卑不亢}地解释了公司的规定。
ctx.en: Faced with the client's awkward demands, she explained company policy with calm dignity.

ctx.s: 爸爸常对我说：“做人要{不卑不亢}，别看不起人，也别怕人。”
ctx.en: Dad often tells me: "Be dignified: don't look down on anyone, and don't be afraid of anyone."

ctx.s: 这位外交官在谈判中{不卑不亢}，赢得了对方的尊重。
ctx.en: The diplomat was neither servile nor overbearing in the talks and earned the other side's respect.

ctx.s: 你觉得他回答记者时的态度算不算{不卑不亢}？
ctx.en: Do you think his manner when answering the reporters counts as dignified?

ctx.s: 那个新来的实习生说话{不卑不亢}，经理对他印象很好。
ctx.en: The new intern speaks with quiet dignity, and the manager was very impressed.

bad.s: 这家餐厅的菜味道{不卑不亢}，还不错。
bad.en: (meant: the food is moderate, not too strong)
bad.why: It describes how a person carries themselves toward others, not taste or degree.

bad.s: 他对老师{不卑不亢}，太没礼貌了。
bad.en: (meant: he was rude to the teacher)
bad.why: It is praise for dignified manners; it cannot be used to criticise rudeness.

mean: to one's heart's content; like mad (busy, having fun)

story.text: The phrase comes from the opening lines of the Analects, where Confucius says: to learn and practise it in due time, is that not a pleasure? When friends come from afar, is that not a joy? In the original it is a rhetorical question about joy. Later speakers reused it as a complement of degree meaning 'to an extreme degree', so today people are busy or play 'like mad'.

use.how: Mostly a complement after 得 describing a lively activity taken to the extreme: 忙得不亦乐乎, 玩得不亦乐乎, 吵得不亦乐乎.

near.diff: 乐此不疲 is enjoying something so much one never tires of it, over time; 不亦乐乎 is how intense one moment of activity is.

cue: Before the Spring Festival the whole family rushes about cleaning, shopping and cooking from morning till night. How busy are they?

ctx.s: 孩子们在雪地里玩得{不亦乐乎}。
ctx.en: The kids were having a whale of a time in the snow.

ctx.s: 快过年了，妈妈每天忙得{不亦乐乎}。
ctx.en: With New Year coming, Mum is run off her feet every day.

ctx.s: 他俩为了一道数学题吵得{不亦乐乎}，谁也不让谁。
ctx.en: The two of them argued like mad over a maths problem, neither giving way.

ctx.s: 你看，爷爷在公园里跟老朋友下棋，下得{不亦乐乎}。
ctx.en: Look, Grandpa is playing chess with his old friends in the park, enjoying himself no end.

ctx.s: 搬家那天，我们几个人从早到晚忙得{不亦乐乎}。
ctx.en: On moving day a few of us were frantically busy from morning to night.

ctx.s: 聚会上大家又唱又跳，闹得{不亦乐乎}，直到半夜才散。
ctx.en: At the party everyone sang and danced and made merry like mad until midnight.

bad.s: 这部电影{不亦乐乎}，你一定要去看。
bad.en: (meant: this film is great fun)
bad.why: It does not describe a thing as fun; it follows a verb plus de to say how intensely people are doing something.

bad.s: 葬礼上，大家悲伤得{不亦乐乎}。
bad.en: (meant: everyone was deeply sad at the funeral)
bad.why: It suits lively, bustling activity and carries a light tone; it cannot express grief.

mean: to gain something without working for it

use.how: Predicate or in 想不劳而获 / 不劳而获的人; criticises living off others' work or wanting reward without effort.

near.diff: 坐享其成 is enjoying a result that others worked for; 不劳而获 is the wider wish or habit of getting anything without effort.

cue: A young man keeps buying lottery tickets and chasing easy-money schemes, hoping to get rich without ever doing a day's work. What does he want?

ctx.s: 世界上没有{不劳而获}的好事。
ctx.en: There is no such thing as a free lunch in this world.

ctx.s: 他整天想着{不劳而获}，从来不肯好好工作。
ctx.en: He spends all day dreaming of getting something for nothing and never works properly.

ctx.s: 别相信那种“躺着赚钱”的广告，想{不劳而获}只会上当。
ctx.en: Don't trust those 'earn money lying down' ads; wanting something for nothing only gets you cheated.

ctx.s: 他总想找一份不用干活、工资又高的工作，这不是想{不劳而获}吗？
ctx.en: He keeps looking for a job with high pay and no work; isn't that just wanting something for nothing?

ctx.s: 父母从小就告诉我，{不劳而获}的钱拿着心里不踏实。
ctx.en: My parents taught me as a child that money you didn't work for never sits easy.

ctx.s: 他从小就有{不劳而获}的思想，长大后吃了不少苦头。
ctx.en: He grew up expecting something for nothing, and paid for it dearly as an adult.

bad.s: 这台新洗衣机让我们{不劳而获}地洗衣服。
bad.en: (meant: we can do the laundry effortlessly)
bad.why: It is a moral criticism of taking reward without work, not a way to say a task is easy.

bad.s: 他每天加班到深夜，终于{不劳而获}地升了职。
bad.en: (meant: he worked late every night and finally earned a promotion)
bad.why: It means gaining without working, so it contradicts the hard work described; it is also a criticism, never praise.

mean: to have the same idea independently

use.how: Predicate, usually with 跟/与…不谋而合 or 我们的想法不谋而合; said of ideas, plans or views that coincide without prior discussion.

near.diff: 异口同声 is saying the same words at the same moment; 不谋而合 is ideas or plans matching without any prior discussion.
一拍即合 is agreeing instantly once someone proposes; 不谋而合 is reaching the same idea separately before talking.

cue: You and a friend, without talking about it, each bought the same book as a present for your teacher. How did your choices relate?

ctx.s: 我们俩的想法{不谋而合}，都想去云南旅行。
ctx.en: We both had the same idea without talking: we each wanted to travel to Yunnan.

ctx.s: 没想到你的方案跟我的{不谋而合}！
ctx.en: I never expected your plan to match mine so exactly!

ctx.s: 两位科学家在不同的国家研究，结论却{不谋而合}。
ctx.en: The two scientists worked in different countries, yet independently reached the same conclusion.

ctx.s: “你也打算辞职创业？”“是啊，看来咱们{不谋而合}。”
ctx.en: "You're planning to quit and start a business too?" "Yes, looks like we had the same idea."

ctx.s: 他提出的建议与经理心里的打算{不谋而合}，当场就被采纳了。
ctx.en: His suggestion happened to match exactly what the manager had in mind and was adopted on the spot.

ctx.s: 这位作家的观点，和古人的看法竟然{不谋而合}。
ctx.en: This writer's view turns out to coincide with that of the ancients.

bad.s: 我们开了三次会，最后终于{不谋而合}了。
bad.en: (meant: after three meetings we finally agreed)
bad.why: It means matching without consulting; an agreement reached through discussion is not a coincidence of ideas.

bad.s: 我{不谋而合}他的看法。
bad.en: (meant: my view is the same as his)
bad.why: It takes no object; say that my view and his matched, with the views as the subject.

use.how: Predicate of 后果 or a clause: (否则)后果不堪设想。 Said of what would happen if something went wrong; often after 如果/要是/否则.

near.diff: 不可思议 is amazing or hard to believe, good or bad; 不堪设想 is only a dreadful outcome that might happen.

cue: A driver nodded off at the wheel and woke just before hitting a lorry. What would the consequences have been if he hadn't woken up?

ctx.s: 幸亏发现得早，不然后果{不堪设想}。
ctx.en: Luckily it was spotted early; otherwise the consequences would have been too dreadful to think about.

ctx.s: 开车时千万别看手机，出了事后果{不堪设想}。
ctx.en: Never look at your phone while driving; if something happens the consequences are unthinkable.

ctx.s: 要是那天孩子没被拉住，真是{不堪设想}啊！
ctx.en: If the child hadn't been grabbed that day, it doesn't bear thinking about!

ctx.s: 如果大坝出现裂缝而无人发现，下游的情况将{不堪设想}。
ctx.en: If the dam cracked and no one noticed, the situation downstream would be too terrible to imagine.

ctx.s: 医生说，再晚送来一个小时，结果就{不堪设想}了。
ctx.en: The doctor said that had he been brought in an hour later, the outcome would not bear thinking about.

ctx.s: 泄露客户资料的后果{不堪设想}，你想过没有？
ctx.en: The consequences of leaking client data would be dreadful; have you thought about that?

bad.s: 这个计划成功的话，收益{不堪设想}。
bad.en: (meant: the profit would be beyond imagining)
bad.why: It only describes terrible outcomes, never good ones; huge gains need a different expression.

bad.s: 他小时候的生活很苦，{不堪设想}。
bad.en: (meant: his childhood was unimaginably hard)
bad.why: It is about a dreadful outcome that could happen, not hardship already lived through.

lit: not taking it to be so (not thinking it right)

use.how: Predicate or adverbial, often 对…不以为然 or 不以为然地摇摇头; shows disagreement with a view, often unspoken or mildly dismissive.

near.diff: 不以为意 is not taking something seriously or not minding it; 不以为然 is thinking a view is wrong.

cue: Your colleague says remote work makes people lazy. You don't agree, and you just give a small shake of the head. How do you feel about his claim?

ctx.s: 他说这部电影很好看，我却{不以为然}。
ctx.en: He said the film was great, but I wasn't convinced.

ctx.s: 听了我的建议，奶奶{不以为然}地摇了摇头。
ctx.en: Hearing my suggestion, Grandma shook her head, unconvinced.

ctx.s: 很多人认为学历最重要，对此我一直{不以为然}。
ctx.en: Many people think qualifications matter most; I have never agreed with that.

ctx.s: “你好像对他的说法{不以为然}？”“嗯，我觉得他说得太绝对了。”
ctx.en: "You don't seem to agree with what he said?" "No, I think he's too absolute."

ctx.s: 专家的预测公布后，不少网友表示{不以为然}。
ctx.en: After the expert's forecast was published, many netizens said they didn't buy it.

ctx.s: 父亲对我选的专业有些{不以为然}，但没有反对。
ctx.en: My father was a little sceptical of the major I chose, but he didn't object.

bad.s: 他发烧了，却{不以为然}，照常去上班。
bad.en: (meant: he had a fever but didn't take it seriously)
bad.why: Not taking something seriously is a different idiom; this one means disagreeing with a view.

bad.s: 我对你的意见{不以为然}，完全同意。
bad.en: (meant: I fully agree with your opinion)
bad.why: It expresses disagreement, so it contradicts saying that you fully agree.

use.how: Predicate of a person who leaves a place or people without a farewell: 他不辞而别了。 Often carries surprise, hurt or blame.

near.diff: 扬长而去 is striding off defiantly in front of others; 不辞而别 is leaving quietly without telling anyone.

cue: A housemate packed up during the night and moved out without a word to anyone. What did he do?

ctx.s: 他昨晚{不辞而别}，连张纸条都没留。
ctx.en: He left last night without saying goodbye, not even leaving a note.

ctx.s: 对不起，那天走得太急，{不辞而别}，请你原谅。
ctx.en: I'm sorry I left in such a hurry that day without saying goodbye; please forgive me.

ctx.s: 为什么你要{不辞而别}？大家都在找你！
ctx.en: Why did you leave without a word? Everyone's been looking for you!

ctx.s: 那位保姆干了半年，突然{不辞而别}，家里乱成一团。
ctx.en: The nanny worked for six months, then suddenly left without notice, and the household was thrown into chaos.

ctx.s: 聚会还没结束，他就悄悄{不辞而别}了。
ctx.en: Before the party was over he had quietly slipped away without saying goodbye.

ctx.s: 小说里，男主角{不辞而别}，只在桌上留下一封信。
ctx.en: In the novel the hero leaves without a farewell, leaving only a letter on the table.

bad.s: 他跟大家一一握手告别后，{不辞而别}了。
bad.en: (meant: he said goodbye to everyone and left)
bad.why: It means leaving without a farewell, so it contradicts saying goodbye first.

bad.s: 他上个月{不辞而别}了这家公司。
bad.en: (meant: last month he left this company without saying goodbye)
bad.why: It takes no object; the place left must come before it with a preposition (from this company), not after it.

use.how: Predicate or attributive with 的, said of a thing or person that something cannot do without: 水是生命不可或缺的。 The subject is the needed thing.

near.diff: Almost the same meaning; 必不可少 is a little plainer and more common in speech, 不可或缺 more written.

cue: In a report on the team, you want to say that one quiet engineer is someone the project simply could not run without.

ctx.s: 手机已经成了生活中{不可或缺}的东西。
ctx.en: The mobile phone has become something we can't do without in daily life.

ctx.s: 在这个团队里，她是{不可或缺}的一员。
ctx.en: On this team she is an indispensable member.

ctx.s: 阳光和水分对植物的生长来说都{不可或缺}。
ctx.en: Sunlight and water are both indispensable to a plant's growth.

ctx.s: 你觉得在一段友谊中，什么是{不可或缺}的？
ctx.en: What do you think is indispensable in a friendship?

ctx.s: 诚信是企业长期发展{不可或缺}的基础。
ctx.en: Integrity is an indispensable foundation for a company's long-term growth.

ctx.s: 对南方人来说，米饭是每顿饭里{不可或缺}的主食。
ctx.en: For southerners, rice is the staple that no meal can be without.

bad.s: 他{不可或缺}这本词典。
bad.en: (meant: he can't do without this dictionary)
bad.why: It takes no object; the needed thing is the subject: the dictionary is indispensable to him.

bad.s: 他每天都{不可或缺}地迟到。
bad.en: (meant: he is late every day without fail)
bad.why: It means something is indispensable, not that something happens without fail.

mean: sparing no effort (to promote or support)

use.how: Adverbial with 地 before verbs like 支持, 帮助, 推广, 宣传: 不遗余力地支持. Said of sustained effort for a cause, a person or a plan.

near.diff: 全力以赴 is throwing everything into one's own task or contest; 不遗余力 is sustained effort to support or promote something.

cue: For twenty years an old teacher has used every spare hour and all his savings to help poor village children go to school. How has he helped them?

ctx.s: 这些年，父母一直{不遗余力}地支持我的梦想。
ctx.en: All these years my parents have spared no effort in supporting my dream.

ctx.s: 老校长{不遗余力}地帮助山区孩子上学。
ctx.en: The old headmaster spared no effort helping children from the mountains go to school.

ctx.s: 他退休后仍{不遗余力}地推广传统书法。
ctx.en: Even after retiring he works tirelessly to promote traditional calligraphy.

ctx.s: 政府表示将{不遗余力}地保护这片湿地。
ctx.en: The government says it will spare no effort to protect this wetland.

ctx.s: 为了让新产品打开市场，公司在宣传上{不遗余力}。
ctx.en: To open up the market for the new product, the company has spared no effort on promotion.

ctx.s: 你真的相信他会{不遗余力}地帮你吗？
ctx.en: Do you really believe he'll do everything he can to help you?

bad.s: 这个箱子太重了，我搬得{不遗余力}。
bad.en: (meant: I carried it with all my strength)
bad.why: It is not a complement of degree and does not describe one physical exertion; it is sustained effort for a cause.

bad.s: 这次考试很简单，我{不遗余力}就通过了。
bad.en: (meant: the exam was easy and I passed effortlessly)
bad.why: It means putting every ounce of effort into something, the opposite of doing it effortlessly.
